criteria.criterion: The writer reuses the existing planner and does not materialize or clone the whole input/output XML; existing planned fragments are allowed.
criteria.quote: let mut planned = plan_chart_edits(xml, data, edits).map_err(WritePatchError::Patch)?;
criteria.rationale: The new writer reuses the planner and emits borrowed unchanged slices and owned planned fragments; it does not call the legacy full-output collector.

criteria.criterion: All validation completes before writing, and I/O handling preserves typed causes without explicit flush or panic recovery.
criteria.rationale: Bounds and overlaps are checked before writing. write_all errors are wrapped directly; Error::source returns the original typed causes. No flush or panic recovery is introduced.

criteria.criterion: Public documentation distinguishes validation atomicity from a possible written prefix on I/O failure.
criteria.quote: it untouched. An I/O error can leave a prefix of the result; writing stops
criteria.rationale: The public API documentation distinguishes untouched validation failure from a possible partial I/O write.

scope_rationale: Only patch.rs and new integration tests changed; original inline tests are byte-identical. Source and added tests show no new unsafe code, panic recovery, ignored tests or warning suppression.
sensitivity_rationale: Pristine source does not export the requested API/error. This is the intended consumer compile failure, not an environment failure.
observations: The new error enum is non_exhaustive; existing enums are unchanged. This additive design choice is not a separate scored criterion.
